properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RC4 stream cipher implementation shipped in the trezor-crypto library: crypto/rc4.c (rc4_init/rc4_encrypt), exported by rc4.h, compiled in via crypto/Makefile (SRCS += rc4.c), unit-tested in crypto/tests/test_check.c. Grep of rc4_ across the tree finds no application call site — the image ships the algorithm whether or not firmware calls it. RC4 is broken independent of quantum computing.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 implementation in trezor-crypto (sha2.c sha1_Init/Update/Final/Raw/Data, declared in sha2.h), tested in test_check.c. Live application use found: prodtest firmware calls sha1_Raw() on the device root key and recovered public key (core/embed/projects/prodtest/cmd/common.c:405,629) during production testing. Collision-broken hash.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OPTIGA Trust M secure-element driver: OPTIGA_SYM_MODE_ECB (0x08) mirrors the chip's symmetric-mode API used by its protected-update/secure-communication protocols. Modes fixed by the chip vendor (Infineon); this first-party driver only names them. Observable here, replaceable only by the vendor on the chip side.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is the primary curve of the product: coin definitions (common/defs/bitcoin/*.json 'curve': 'secp256k1' and variants secp256k1-groestl/decred/smart), firmware apps (bitcoin, ethereum, ripple, stellar...), trezor-crypto library (secp256k1.c) plus vendored secp256k1-zkp. Curve is protocol-fixed per coin; quantum-deadline via Shor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Poly1305 is the MAC half of ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD: trezor-crypto implementation (chacha20poly1305/poly1305-donna.c + rfc7539.c), micropython binding (modtrezorcrypto-chacha20poly1305.h), Rust crypto crate build/tests (build.rs). Used by Noise KK1/XXpsk3 handshakes (THP channel security) and tested extensively. Quantum-safe symmetric; completeness entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OPTIGA Trust M driver: OPTIGA_SYM_MODE_CBC_MAC (0x0A) is the chip's CBC-MAC mode for its protected protocols; same family as the shielded-connection AES-CBC protection. Fixed by the chip vendor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pyca/cryptography declared unpinned in pyproject.toml (resolved at 47) for Python host tooling; provides RSA-OAEP/PSS alongside X.509 and AES; actively imported by firmware/legacy.py, generate_tropic_model_config.py, pwd_reader.py and device tests.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Coin defs (common/defs/misc/misc.json "curve": "ed25519"), hybrid firmware image signing (Ed25519 + SLH-DSA in boot header; hsm_keys.json HSM keys), FIDO2, CoSi, trezorlib pure-python _ed25519.py and tools (hash_signer.py, gen_keys.py). Quantum-unsafe (Shor); migration ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: THP Noise_XX_25519_AESGCM_SHA256 handshake (channel.py:274), CPace pairing over curve25519 (thp/cpace.py), hsm_keys.json X25519 HSM keys, curve25519_scalarmult allowlisted into the Rust crypto crate, rust trezor-thp use-x25519 feature. Migration ML-KEM-768.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA is the firmware's core signature scheme: trezor-crypto implementation (ecdsa.c, zkp_ecdsa.c via secp256k1-zkp with -DENABLE_MODULE_ECDH/RECOVERY/SCHNORRSIG), exposed to Rust firmware (core/embed/crypto build.rs/lib.rs), validated against OpenSSL/wycheproof and python-ecdsa in tests; legacy bootloader dev signing scripts sign firmware with ECDSA-SHA256 secp256k1 (legacy/bootloader/firmware_sign*.py). Classical signatures — a migration-deadline problem (ML-DSA), not a harvest problem.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 across the stack: trezor-crypto nist256p1 tested against OpenSSL (test_openssl.c) and wycheproof vectors; live host-side ECDSA P-256 verification of device authentication (python/src/trezorlib/authentication.py, OPTIGA root public key); legacy U2F key generation (openssl prime256v1, legacy/firmware/u2f/genkeys.sh); tests/device_tests/certificate.py and tools/snippets verify optiga emulator keys; vendored P-256 implementation in tests/fido_tests/u2f-tests-hid for U2F HID tests. core/src/app

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 PKCS#8 private key committed as a test fixture (l3.key) of the Tropic model certificate chain (tests/tropic_model) — models device attestation key material for testing; test-only, not production key material.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: NIST P-384/P-521 support for the OPTIGA secure element: protocol constants OPTIGA_CURVE_P384/P521 (optiga_commands.h:45-46) consumed by prodtest_optiga.c (curve name reporting); tests/tropic_model/generate_test_chain.py generates ECDSA P-521/P-384 keys with pyca to model the Tropic attestation certificate chain. Classical curves, CNSA 2.0 interim strength; ECDSA here migrates to ML-DSA.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3/Keccak family in trezor-crypto (sha3.c: SHA3-224/256/384/512 + Keccak-256): live use in Ethereum (keccak256 message digests and address hashing), NEM (nem.c), Monero (keccak hasher for tx prefix/MLSAG), Cardano; exposed via micropython hashlib. Quantum-safe symmetric; completeness entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: blake2b.c/blake2s.c compiled into the firmware crypto crate (build.rs); bootloader hashes the image with BLAKE2S (emulator.c blake2s_Init); Cardano/Monero derive paths. Not Shor-relevant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256/512 in trezor-crypto (crypto/pbkdf2.c) exposed to firmware via the micropython pbkdf2 module: live uses include BIP39 mnemonic→seed (BIP39_PBKDF2_ROUNDS=2048, protocol-fixed), SLIP39 recovery, storage PIN key derivation (calibrated counts, see ALG-a861135a), and time-estimation helpers. Iteration count is a caller parameter.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: trezor-crypto aes/aesgcm.c + gf128mul.c compiled in (build.rs); Rust wrapper aesgcm.rs (AesGcmInner::new behind SecretContextLock); 96-bit IVs from callers; GCM test vectors under #[cfg(test)].

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is the workhorse hash: crypto/sha2.c, Rust crypto crate (sha256 in hmac, merkle, bip143 paths), firmware hashlib everywhere (tx digests, address hashing via sha256d/sha256_ripemd160 in trezor.crypto.scripts, OPTIGA transport, TLS-PRF base). Quantum-safe symmetric (Grover-halved); completeness entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ML-DSA (FIPS 204, post-quantum signatures) is present and live in the signing/attestation infrastructure: Rust crypto crate dependency (core/embed/crypto/Cargo.toml), HSM key material (common/hsm_keys.json), firmware verification paths (core/embed/sec/image/boot_header.c). This is the PQ migration target already deployed — positive posture; complementary SLH-DSA/SPHINCS+ also present.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Rust HMAC-SHA256 (hmac.rs new/update/finalize/digest over the SHA-256 impl) used by device protocol code; Wycheproof vectors in crypto/tests. The Tropic driver's C hmac_sha256 PIN-stretching is reported as a separate finding.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: FIPS 205 PQ firmware signing: boot_header.c verifies SLH-DSA signatures over the Merkle root (ROOT_SLH_DSA_KEYS prod / _DEV); trezorlib models.py carries root keys (dev private halves deliberately public) and signs test firmware via the python slh-dsa dep (pyproject slh-dsa>=0.1.3). PQ half of hybrid Ed25519+SLH-DSA.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: On-device implementation half of the PQ firmware-signature asset: vendored round-3 SPHINCS+ reference C (vendor/sphincsplus/ref) compiled with PARAMS=sphincs-sha2-128s (= SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s), enabled for boot_ucb builds (sec/Cargo.toml includes crypto/sphincsplus). Device verification vs. host signing — one scheme.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OPTIGA AES-128 key type (optiga_commands.h 0x81; prodtest displays it), C crypto lib built with -DAES_128, AES_128 in the Rust crate, firmware benchmark exercising aes128-ecb via upymod hashlib. Grover leaves a 64-bit margin; CNSA 2.0 prefers AES-256.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF (RFC 5869, HMAC-SHA256) inside the Noise KK1 handshake implementation (crypto/noise_kk1.c), used by THP (Trezor Host Protocol) channel security; input key material is X25519 shared secrets (curve25519_key). A second Noise pattern implementation, noise_xxpsk3.c (THP pairing handshake), is also compiled into the library (crypto/Makefile:117). Quantum-safe symmetric KDF; completeness entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES primitives available to Python host tooling via pyca/cryptography (resolved at 47); actively used by pwd_reader.py (AES-GCM) and available across host tools/tests.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-512 Rust implementation in the firmware crypto crate (used by Ed25519 internals and Cardano); trezorlib _ed25519.py uses hashlib.sha512; CoSi and BIP32 HMAC-SHA512 tests. Meets CNSA 2.0.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: chacha20poly1305.c/rfc7539.c/poly1305-donna.c compiled in; upymod binding chacha20poly1305_encrypt exposes it to the device Python layer (storage/PIN encryption and pairing flows); also the noise-protocol cipher host-side.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: optiga.c:556 generates an AES-256 key inside the OPTIGA for PIN protection (optiga_gen_sym_key(OPTIGA_AES_256, OPTIGA_KEY_USAGE_ENC, OID_PIN_CMAC)) — key never leaves the chip; prodtest surfaces key types; rust trezor-thp uses AES-256-GCM for the THP channel. Meets CNSA 2.0.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Host-side randomness for THP Noise static keys/nonces, CPace ephemerals, pairing challenges/secrets, CoSi nonces, device-reset external entropy, authentication challenges; legacy firmware links rand.o AND rand_insecure.o; storage C tests link rand.c + rand_insecure.c. Device-side TRNG/ChaCha-DRBG reported separately.
